t: Section 205(a) of the Sugar Act of 1948, as amended, is amended by striking out the third sentence and inserting in lieu thereof the following: “The Secretary is authorized in making such allotments, whenever there is involved any allotment that pertains to a new or substantially enlarged existing sugar beet processing facility serving a locality or localities which have received an acreage allotment under section 302(b) (3) or that pertains to a sugar beet processing facility described in section 302(b)(9), to take into consideration in lieu of or in addition to the foregoing factors of processing, past marketings and ability to market, the need for establishing an allotment which will permit such marketing of sugar as is necessary for reasonably efficient operation of any such sugar beet processing facility during each of the first three, years of its operation.”

fable.w: The section only authorizes the Secretary to weigh an additional factor (the need for efficient operation of new sugar beet processing facilities) when making marketing allotments. The tempting reading is that allotments affecting processors and localities imply outside involvement, but the text provides no hearing, comment period, consultation, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. The decision stays entirely with the Secretary.
fable.s: The Secretary is authorized in making such allotments

qwen_block.w: This section grants the Secretary discretion to consider specific economic factors (efficient operation of processing facilities) when making acreage allotments. It does not require consultation with outside parties, public comment, or the involvement of non-federal entities in the decision-making process. The 'consideration' is an internal analytical step by the federal official, not a participatory mechanism involving outsiders.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary is authorized in making such allotments... to take into consideration... the need for establishing an allotment which will permit such marketing of sugar as is necessary for reasonably efficient operation of any such sugar beet processing facility

opus.w: This amendment only adds a factor the Secretary may consider when setting sugar marketing allotments: what a new or enlarged beet processing facility needs to run efficiently. It does not create any consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. Any hearing requirement elsewhere in section 205(a) is not stated in this text. The processing facilities are affected by the decision but do not take part in making it.
opus.s: The Secretary is authorized in making such allotments, whenever there is involved any allotment that pertains to a new or substantially enlarged existing sugar beet processing facility
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** This amends a statute about the Secretary's allotment decisions. Section 205(a) of the Sugar Act, read as a whole, may already involve notice and hearing before allotments are made. That could make the amendment look like part of a participatory process. But nothing in this section's text mentions a hearing, comment period, consultation, rulemaking, or any outside party taking part in the decision. The text only adds a factor the Secretary may weigh: the needs of new or enlarged sugar beet processing facilities. The processing facilities are the subjects of the allotment, not participants in deciding it.
